# Verifying a vocabulary fix with before-and-after tic rates — facts

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] EQ-Bench's Slop Score is a weighted composite (60% slop words, 25% not-X-but-Y patterns, 15% slop trigrams) computed against human baselines (wordfreq for words, a human essay/creative corpus for trigrams); it is not an AI-vs-human classifier and may underreport outside creative writing and essays. (medium confidence) — https://eqbench.com/slop-score.html · keywords: Verifying a vocabulary fix with before-and-after tic rates · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19163v1
- [statement] Arena's baseline counts on Opus 5 (510 vs 158 words per response against Opus 4.5, em dashes 2.3x, 'load-bearing' about 2x, sentences 58% longer) show per-response rates that can serve as a before figure, but the guide's fix was written for Fable 5.1 and nothing shows it works on Opus 5. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-12) — https://paddo.dev/blog/a-dial-worth-turning/ · keywords: Verifying a vocabulary fix with before-and-after tic rates

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Verbal Tic Index (VTI) combines TicRate (share of responses containing a tic), MATTR lexical diversity, a sycophancy score and phrase repetition rate with weights 0.3/0.2/0.3/0.2; the authors say other weights may reorder models, so it is a comparative summary, not an absolute measure. Use response-level tic share as a simple before/after rate. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19139v2 · keywords: Verifying a vocabulary fix with before-and-after tic rates · also: https://eqbench.com/slop-score.html
- [statement] The VTI study is observational (160,000 responses, 8 models); it reports no before/after intervention, so it gives baselines but no evidence of how much a prompt fix reduces tics. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2604.19139v2 · keywords: Verifying a vocabulary fix with before-and-after tic rates · also: https://paddo.dev/blog/a-dial-worth-turning/
- [statement] Anthropic's Fable 5.1 guide supplies a 'mannered prose' definition paragraph (or the short 'Please remove all mannered prose.') to add to a user message or system prompt, and tells users to test against their own evals, but publishes no measured before/after rate for it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-1 · keywords: Verifying a vocabulary fix with before-and-after tic rates · also: https://paddo.dev/blog/a-dial-worth-turning/
- [statement] Automatic lexical metrics only partly capture slop: in a copy-editor annotation study, linear models on available automatic metrics reached AUPRC 0.52-0.55 on news and MS MARCO, and zero-shot GPT-4 judging scored kappa near 0, so a tic-rate drop does not prove the text is better. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19163v1 · keywords: Verifying a vocabulary fix with before-and-after tic rates · also: https://eqbench.com/slop-score.html
